title: Problem definition for maximum product cutting
summary: For a fixed sum, choose how many parts to cut and their sizes to maximize their product.
context: Given an integer n ≥ 2, split n into a sum of m ≥ 2 positive integers n = n₁ + n₂ + … + nₘ (with subscripts 1 through m) so as to maximize the product n₁ × n₂ × … × nₘ.
description: A symbolic bar diagram shows a solid gray bar of total length n above and an equal-length segmented colored bar below cut by vertical dashed lines into n₁, n₂, n₃, …, nₘ₋₂, nₘ₋₁, nₘ (ending at subscripts m minus 2, m minus 1, and m) from left to right, with dashed alignment lines at both ends showing the parts sum to n; below reads "Given integer n, find max(n₁ × n₂ × n₃ × … × nₘ₋₂ × nₘ₋₁ × nₘ)".

frames.title: Problem definition for maximum product cutting
frames.explanation: The subscripted labels and ellipsis represent an arbitrary m-part split rather than requiring at least six parts; m can be as small as 2. Neither n, m, nor concrete part sizes are fixed here, so schematic bar widths do not represent numeric values.
